title: Calibrated Sports web data contract, schema_version 2
description: THE executable contract between jobs/export_web.py (producer) and calibratedsports-web (consumer). docs/web-schema.md is the prose; this file is what runs. The exporter validates every file it writes against it, the site generates lib/schema.generated.ts from it, and CI on both sides fails on drift. Before this existed both sides were hand transcriptions of the prose, and they disagreed: identity.name was typed string while the exporter emitted null, which was a 500 on one page and a browser-side throw on another. additionalProperties is false everywhere a shape is closed, ON PURPOSE - an additive field must fail validation until this file is updated in the same commit, which is what forces the site's types to regenerate. Nothing here names a sport: stat keys, groups, period labels and season types are open strings owned by each sport's manifest.

x-contract.comment: Consumed by jobs/export_web.py and scripts/generate-schema-types.mjs. Both derive their kind list from here rather than hardcoding one.

tables.comment: Keys that are NOT JSON and are not validated by a $def: columnar files a producer appends to. Each entry names its pattern, its format and its columns with their types, and the producer asserts its own column list and types against this entry before it writes, so the two cannot drift. The uploader ships a non-JSON key only when it matches a pattern here, and NEVER deletes one by absence: an append-only file that vanished because one run did not re-declare it would destroy the only record of what was published.

board_ledger.description: The Board's lean ledger: append-only EVENTS, never mutable rows. One `published` event when a lean first appears at a read, and at most one terminal event later - `graded` (result cleared / missed / push) or `void` (with void_reason). A later file must equal the earlier one row for row, plus rows at the end. The CSV is the same rows as the parquet, written in the same step.

Timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC to the second, always Z. Unix seconds live in *_ts fields and are plain numbers.

Interval.description: A [lo, hi] pair. Exactly two numbers, never a bare array of unknown length.

Stats.description: Stat components, keyed by the sport's own stat keys. The keys are NOT enumerated here - that would name a sport. Every key used must be defined in the sport manifest's stat_definitions, which jobs/export_web.assert_stats_defined enforces separately. null means unknown or not collected, never zero.

group.description: Free text owned by the sport. The site orders groups from config/sports/{sport}.ts, not from here.

MarketDefinition.description: One market a prop-history record can name, and how to say it. This is a SECOND vocabulary beside stat_definitions on purpose: a market and a stat are different claims, and the producer already spells them differently - market file components carry stat keys (rec, rush_att, td) while prop_history carries market names (receptions, rush_attempts, anytime_td). Measured 2026-09-18 on the real export: all 8 market names in prop_history are absent from stat_definitions, across 672 players and 25,529 records, and nothing caught it because jobs/export_web.stat_keys_used never walked prop_history - assert_stats_defined accepted a planted nonsense key there while raising on the same key in career.stats.

stat.description: The stat_definitions key this market settles on, or NULL when no published stat is the same claim. Null is a real state and not a gap to be filled later: anytime_td is a binary claim while td is a count, and sacks and tackles_assists settle on columns this sport publishes only inside team splits - measured, not assumed. Pointing a market at a near-miss key would state something false, which is the failure the contract exists to prevent.

note.description: Why stat is null, when it is. Required reading for anyone tempted to fill it in.

TeamSeasonSummary.description: The CURRENT season's figures for one team, computed once at export so an index listing every team costs ONE read instead of opening every team file - the same reason `counts` exists. Which season it describes is `current.season`; it is deliberately not repeated here, because two statements of one fact can disagree. Components, never derived totals: `cleared`/`missed`/`tied` rather than a record string, since integers cannot disagree with each other the way a string and its parts can, and season totals rather than per-game rates, which a reader divides by `games`.

tied.description: Required because the sport has them. A {games, cleared, missed} triple silently loses a drawn result - cleared + missed stops equalling games and nothing says why - so the third outcome is a field rather than an omission.

points_against.description: Null, not zero, before a team has played: no games is not the same statement as no points.

cumulative.description: The season PATH the teams board draws: one entry per regular-season week of the league's schedule (index 1..N, N taken from the schedule), in order. A played week carries the running total THROUGH that week; every other state carries null in every value - never zero, never the previous week carried forward, never a projection. The last played entry equals this summary's own totals; the producer refuses to export otherwise. The chart's axis ceiling is the highest value any team's path reaches, which the reader takes from these arrays rather than from a separately published figure that could disagree with them.

TeamWeekPlayed.description: A week of the season path this team PLAYED: its fixture carries both scores. Every value is cumulative through this week. `cleared` is the chart's wins; `missed` and `tied` travel with it so cleared + missed + tied is the games played to date.

TeamWeekEmpty.description: A week of the season path that carries no value, and WHY - three different facts, none of which is zero. The rule is the team page schedule strip's own, so the chart and the strip cannot disagree: `bye` is the ONE regular-season week up to the team's last scheduled week with no fixture; if there are two or more such weeks the bye is unresolved (a cancelled game looks the same) and each is `gap`, as is any week past the team's last fixture; `unplayed` is a fixture with no result yet, whether or not it has kicked off - that split depends on the reader's clock, and the team file's `kickoff_ts` carries it.

TeamEntry.description: One team in the sport manifest's listing. `conference`, `division` and `classification` are three fields rather than one because the same word means different things across sports: a competitive tier in one, a sub-conference grouping in another. Each is published AS THE SOURCE HOLDS IT and never decomposed - where a source stores a grouping as a single atom, splitting it would invent a structure the sport does not record. All three are nullable and all three are required: a sport states what it has, and says null for what it does not, because an absent key and a null one are different statements.

division.description: The grouping a listing groups by, exactly as the source records it. It may or may not embed the conference - that is the source's choice, not the contract's.

classification.description: The competitive tier, where a sport has one. Null where it does not.

season.description: Current-season figures, or null where the sport publishes none.

TeamMembership.description: One team's grouping in ONE season. Membership is a per-season fact, not a team attribute: 26 teams in one league changed conference between two consecutive seasons, so a single current value cannot describe a historical row. The current season's values live in the manifest, where one fetch answers 'what is the league now'; the history lives here, beside the schedule that already carries per-season truth.

ScoringPreset.description: Scoring is data, not code. The site runs one scoring function over these weights, so a preset and a user's custom scoring share a code path (site-architecture 3.1).

Identity.description: A player as the summary file carries them.

name.description: NULLABLE, and this is the field that caused the 9c8f44b outage. A player can appear in the stat rows with no crosswalk row to name them; the site renders every player name through displayName() (name, else slug).

ids.description: Source ids by system. Open map: a sport brings its own set, and an id that is not known is null rather than absent.

headshot_url.description: https URL hotlinked from the sport's image host, never stored in R2. null when unknown.

jersey_number.description: OPTIONAL, NULLABLE. The number worn in the season of the player's latest stat row (numbers change; the per-season value is on seasons[].jersey_number). A STRING of one or two digits, not an integer, so 0 and 00 stay different numbers. null where the source has no roster for that season, names no number, or names one that is not one or two digits. Optional because a producer adds it only once its source is ingested; absent means not produced, null means not known.

birth_date.description: OPTIONAL, NULLABLE. ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Published as the part, never as an age: the site computes age at read time, so the file does not go stale on a birthday. null when the source does not record it.

ShortIdentity.description: Player season files carry only enough identity to title a page.

MarketIdentity.description: Market files carry no ids/aliases/headshot - the summary file is where those live.

PeriodRow.description: One game. `index` is the period number within its season, in whatever unit the sport manifest's period_type declares.

Fixture.description: One game of the league's current period (a-15). Teams are slugs, as ScheduleGame.opponent is.

home.description: The home team's slug. For a neutral-site game, the team the source designates home.

spread.description: The HOME team's expected margin of victory in points, so the sign is from the HOME team's perspective: positive means the home team is favoured, negative means the away team is favoured, 0 is a pick'em. A home side listed at -3.5 by a sportsbook is +3.5 here - this is NOT the sportsbook convention, in which the favourite carries the minus sign. A producer whose source uses the sportsbook convention must negate it. Null when the source has no line. For a game not yet played it is the source's line at export and can still move.

total.description: The points line on the combined score of both teams. Null when the source has none.

opponent_abbr.description: NULLABLE (finding C-7): the opponent's short code, or null where the feed carries none. In one sport's archive more than half of all opponent sides outside the current era have no abbreviation, mostly opponents from outside the published scope. Null rather than an invented code, because a fabricated abbreviation would look like an identity the sport does not have - and rather than an empty string, which renders as a gap that says nothing about why.

spread.description: From THIS team's perspective: positive means this team is favoured.

slug.description: NULLABLE: a roster lists everyone who played, but only players in the export's scope get a page and therefore a slug. 63.5% of roster rows carry null here. lib/schema.ts typed this `string` until this contract was written - the same class of lie as identity.name, not yet fired only because the site dereferences it behind has_page.

games.description: NULLABLE (finding C-4): games the player appeared in, or null where the sport has no appearance signal at all. A sport that records whether a player dressed answers this with a number. A sport that does not can only count games carrying a stat row, which is a LOWER BOUND that reads as an appearance count - on one real roster it is 0 for nearly the whole squad. The asymmetry is the argument: every share beside it was already nullable and degrades honestly, while the one field that could not be null was the one a sport may be unable to produce. A confident 0 is a worse answer than no answer. The measurements behind this live in docs/web-schema.md, which may name a sport; this document may not.

has_page.description: True when this player is in scope and has their own page. When true, slug is non-null.

defense_snap_share.description: OPTIONAL, NULLABLE. Mean per-game DEFENSIVE snap share, computed exactly as snap_share is. snap_share is OFFENSIVE snaps only, so a defender or specialist reads 0 there beside the games he played; this is the figure that belongs beside it. null where the sport's snap feed has no row for the player's games.

Basis.description: How a component was priced. MARKET is quoted directly, DERIVED is computed from another component, ANCHORED is scaled from a rate fitted elsewhere. Publishing this per component is mandatory - a derived yardage number must never read as a market price.

allOf.description: A MARKET component must show the ladder it was priced from, even when that ladder is empty and a note explains why. DERIVED and ANCHORED must not carry rungs - they were not quoted.

PricePath.description: How ONE rung's price moved, for drawing a curve. Lossless change-points, not a downsample: these series are step functions - a rung carries ~143 quotes but only 35-59 actual changes and 11-19 distinct values - so every retained point is a real observation and nothing between them is invented. A curve-fitting downsample (LTTB and friends) would reposition points onto triangle-optimal picks and round a discrete jump into a gradual slope, which is precisely what the chart must not show. One series per market, the rung nearest the posted line; the survival curve is the complementary view showing every rung at one instant.

market_id.description: The venue instrument, so the path is traceable to its source.

first_quote_ts.description: DERIVED from the series - the first quote actually seen, never an assumed listing time. For these markets it happens to be listing, which will not generalise.

dropped.description: Changes omitted to fit the point cap, smallest magnitude first. Omitting a 1c wobble is honest; inventing a point is not - so this counts omissions and there is no interpolation anywhere. Normally 0.

ts.description: Real timestamp. Plot time on x - even spacing would make a sharp repricing look gradual.

Verdict.description: A hypothesis's standing. `edge_confirmed` exists so the programme's headline - that nothing found an edge surviving costs - is FALSIFIABLE: computed over an enum without it, that count could never have come out otherwise, which makes it decoration rather than a finding. Its criterion is strict and stated here so assigning it is a check, not a judgement: the interval on net-of-cost CLV excludes zero AND the result replicates on a holdout the mechanism was frozen before. R11 (022 H1, settlement lag, +1.81pp [+1.24, +2.47]) is the only hypothesis that clears the first half; it stays `open` because it fails the second - week-2 replication - which is what the value being reachable is supposed to mean.

script.description: The committed script that produces the number. Anything quoted as a finding must have one.

wilson.description: Wilson interval, not a normal approximation - the buckets are small and the rates are low.

SportManifest.description: The only mutable pointer the site polls, and the only place stat labels, formats, groups and scoring weights exist.

period_type.description: What a period IS for this sport, declared by the sport itself - a week, a game, a date. Nothing in the contract assumes any of them.

stale.description: True when the source is late: data_through lags the last completed period. The site shows a banner rather than silently serving old numbers.

fixtures.description: Every game of `period`, league-wide, in kickoff order (a-15). OPTIONAL: absent means this producer does not publish fixtures, which is a different statement from an empty list - a period with no games.

market_definitions.description: Labels for the market keys prop_history uses, keyed by market key. Without this the site has no way to word a prop-history row: it reads stat names that stat_definitions does not define, so it can render a rate and not what the rate is about.

teams.description: Every team this sport publishes, carrying the current-season grouping and figures a listing needs. Extended 2026-09-19 for track B's A14 and track C's C-3: it was {slug, abbr, name} and nothing else, so one figure per team meant opening every team file on an index page - precisely the cost `counts` was exported to remove.

team_colors.description: Team colours keyed on the abbreviation AS PUBLISHED, not the current franchise: STL, SD and OAK are separate entries from LA, LAC and LV, so a game keeps the identity it was played under. Colours only - a hex value is a fact about a team, a logo is a trademark. Sourced from the sport's own reference feed, never hand-typed. Wider than `teams`, which lists the current franchises that have pages.

counts.description: Coverage, computed once at export so a page costs one read. games and rungs exist because the site otherwise had to open 32 team files or all 11 market files to state them, which is the cost the components table exists to remove.

games.description: Games with a final score. NOT every scheduled row: the table carries fixtures that have not been played (256 of 7,548 at the time of writing), and a coverage figure counting them would claim a record the site does not hold.

rungs.description: Ladder rungs across every published market file, summed over components. The market count says how many players are priced; this says how much of a curve each price rests on.

unresolved_ids.description: Ids the export could not fully resolve, and why - including players excluded from the export for having no resolvable name. Published so an exclusion is visible on the site rather than being a silent filter.

PlayerSummary.description: First paint: identity, the season list, aggregates and the market pointer. No game logs - those are per-season files.

jersey_number.description: OPTIONAL, NULLABLE. The number worn that season, as a one- or two-digit string - the season's last roster week that names one, so a player traded mid-season shows the number he finished in. null where no roster names one.

market.description: Pointer to this period's market file, or null when there is no current-period market.

prop_history.description: The settled prop record, or null for a player with none. 672 of 3,970 exported players have one; the 681 with settled props and no page are defenders, whose stats are not exported at player level yet.

PropHistoryStat.description: One stat's settled record. `priority` marks the markets the research settled on (targets, rush attempts, receptions); it is DATA so the site can word the ordering rather than hard-coding a claim about it. `n` counts posted lines and `games` counts the independent events behind them - a ladder prices several thresholds on one player-game and they all settle off the same final stat line, so `rate` is over `n` while the INTERVAL is over `games`. Quote games alongside any comparison: n alone overstates the evidence by up to 10x on receiving yards. rate and interval are null at n = 0.

PropHistoryRecord.description: One (season, stat, line) claim. The line is part of the identity: a ladder prices several thresholds in one game and they are different claims, so collapsing them would average away the record.

PropHistory.description: The settled prop record: how often the OVER cleared. A FACT, not a pick - per the editorial line, hit-rate history is publishable and a recommendation is not. It needs no closing price, only the posted line and the settled result, which is why it covers the current season while market-comparison figures cannot. Each market is counted ONCE: a settled prop is stored twice in the producer (over and under) carrying the same market-level result, so counting both would leave the rate right and double n. `stats` is ordered, priority markets first.

memberships.description: This team's grouping per season. The CURRENT season's values live in the sport manifest, so a listing costs one fetch; the history lives here, beside the schedule that already carries per-season truth. May be empty where a sport publishes no membership history - an empty array is an honest statement that none is published, which is a different thing from the key being absent.

MarketFile.description: A market-implied fantasy distribution for one player-period. Every component carries its basis, and the validation note travels with the file - the method was validated on sportsbook ladders and the exchange arm was not.

as_of.description: The freshest quote the distribution was built from, NOT when the file was written.

path.description: This market's price over time, or null when no series exists. Exactly one series - other rungs are deliberately NOT published: nine overlaid lines are an unreadable chart, and the contract being closed means adding one later fails loudly rather than the site silently expecting a field nothing writes.

distributions.description: Keyed by the manifest's scoring preset keys. Replaced in site-architecture 3.2 by marginals plus a correlation matrix sampled in the browser, which is what makes custom scoring possible.

model_minus_naive.description: Paired difference against the naive prior-season rate, same game-block bootstrap and THE SAME POPULATION as `model_minus_market` and as the three Brier scores above - all of them the common set named in `population`. Two intervals on different denominators are not comparable, and a consumer gating "identical to naive" on model == naive must be able to read the interval beside it from the same rows.

Availability.description: Can this metric answer a question about the CURRENT season? `historical` is not a defect - a participation-derived metric structurally cannot, because that feed refreshes only after the postseason - but it has to be said rather than discovered when a live page renders an empty panel. Derived from the metric's measured coverage, not declared: the producer refuses `current` on a metric whose inputs stop before the live season.

SharedDenominator.description: What two SUBJECTS divide, when they divide anything. `team` is any share-of-team figure - target share, carry share, snap share - where two teammates split one total and their shares are therefore mechanically opposed; two such intervals rendered side by side are not two independent estimates and the page must say so. `own` means the denominator is the subject's own total (an air-yard bin share divides that player's targets), so nothing is shared and the caveat does not apply. `null` means the metric is not a share at all. `own` is an explicit answer, not a default: the producer refuses a share-shaped metric that leaves this unset.

AnalyticValue.description: One published number, its interval and its sample. THE INTERVAL AND `n` ARE REQUIRED AND NOT NULLABLE - that is the whole point of this kind. Every stats site publishes point estimates; publishing the uncertainty is what makes these ours, and expressing the rule here means the CONSUMER refuses a bare rate rather than trusting the producer's own gate. `n` is INDEPENDENT UNITS - games, or players - never rows: a player's targets inside one game share a game plan, and counting rows as the sample makes an interval roughly sqrt(rows-per-block) too narrow.

subject.description: A gsis_id, a team abbreviation, or `_league` for a league-wide figure.

slice.description: The bucket within the metric, or "" for the headline value. What it means is given once by the metric's `slice_kind`.

n.description: Independent units the interval was built on, not rows. Never zero: nothing measured is not a value.

rows.description: Raw observations, when they exceed `n`. Published beside it because the gap between them is usually an order of magnitude and only one of the two is the sample.

method.description: How the interval was constructed - `block2000`, `hist2000`, `wilson95`, `t95`. An interval hides its own construction; this does not.

AnalyticMetricFile.description: One analytic: what it measures, the range over which it can be trusted, and every value. The range fields are on the ENVELOPE and never repeated per value - repeating them is the duplication that lets two copies disagree.

unit.description: What the number IS, in words. A page renders this rather than inventing a caption.

block.description: What the interval resamples - the unit of independence.

basis.description: Which feed it is computed from: pbp, participation, ngs. A participation-derived metric can never serve the current season.

slice_kind.description: What `slice` means for this metric - a script bucket, a down bucket, a season, an air-yard bin - or "" when the metric has a single headline value. One long value table serves every analytic, so without this a reader cannot tell a slice of "2019" from a slice of "3rd_short".

range_note.description: Why the range is what it is, in words, naming the input that bounds it. DERIVED from measured coverage, not typed: a hand-written bound stops being true when upstream moves and nothing notices.

requires.description: The measured columns the range was derived from, as `dataset.column` or `dataset.column|condition`.

AnalyticsIndexEntry.description: A metric as a LISTING needs it. Deliberately not a copy of the metric envelope - it carries what a list renders plus where to fetch the rest.

key.description: The data key holding this metric's values.

AnalyticsIndexFile.description: Every analytic available for a sport, with its usable range, so a page can list them without fetching each one.

source.description: The store and build the figures came from, so a number on a page can be traced to one.

LivePrice.description: One exchange market as the producer last READ it. Every price carries the moment it was true. Nothing here is derived - no mid, no de-vig - because the consumer already derives the mid only where both sides are quoted, and a second derivation is a second place to disagree.

event.description: The venue's event identifier, which groups the markets of one game.

bid.description: Best bid to buy YES, as a probability. Null when nothing is bid. 0 and 1 are never emitted: on an exchange contract they are not quotes.

ask.description: Best price to buy YES, as a probability - the complement of the best NO bid. Null when nothing is offered.

read_at.description: When this price was read from the venue: the START of the poll that read it, so never later than the truth. Not the publish time and not the upload time.

expected_every_s.description: The cadence this market was being polled at when it was read. Age is judged against THIS: ten minutes is normal on a 600 s cadence and a stall on a 10 s one.

close_at.description: When the venue closes the market, if known.

in_catalogue.description: True while the venue still lists the market as open; false once it has left the open list, after which this is the LAST price read and it will not update. Null until the producer has seen a catalogue at all.

LivePricesFile.description: Exchange prices published by the capture process on a short cycle, so the site reads storage instead of calling the venue. A FAILURE IS A STALE FILE, so the file states its own age: generated_at is when it was written, stale_after is the deadline for the next write, and each price carries its own read_at. The consumer decides what to render; this shape only makes the age impossible to miss.

source.description: How the prices were obtained, in words - a live capture, or a staged copy from storage.

series.description: The venue series this file covers. Nothing outside them is included.

publish_every_s.description: How often the producer checks for a newer read to publish.

heartbeat_s.description: The longest the producer goes without writing, even when no price was re-read.

stale_after.description: generated_at + heartbeat + one cycle + a small grace. Past this, the producer has stopped writing and every price in the file is unconfirmed, however recent its read_at looks.

two_sided.description: Markets with both a bid and an ask.

omitted.description: Markets held but left out by the size cap, nearest close kept first. Counted so a cap is never a silent filter.

ComponentsPlayer.description: Enough identity to title and link a row. The full identity is on the player's summary.

ComponentsRow.description: One player in one period. `values` is positional against the file's `columns` and always the same length. Each value means what Stats means: null is unknown or not collected, never zero, and 0 is a recorded zero.

index.description: The period number within the season, as PeriodRow.index.

ComponentsFile.description: THE COMPONENTS TABLE: one season of per-player, per-period stat components for the whole league in one file, so a page can sort every player on one key and score them under any weights. It is a projection of the player season files - the same rows, the same nulls - laid out as columns so it stays small enough to load in a browser. Components only: no total, per-game rate or fantasy score is stored, because each is a sum or ratio the page computes, and scoring bonuses apply per period so a stored season total could not be scored. `columns` are stat keys defined in the sport manifest's stat_definitions. A share over any span is sum(part) / sum(denominator) using the denominator columns published beside it, never a mean of per-period shares.

CoverageFile.description: What this project HOLDS, per sport, read from the stores at `generated_at`. One file for every sport, so a sport's status cannot say one thing on its own coming-soon page and another on the home page. Every count here was read from the table it describes by jobs/export_coverage.py; none is typed. `sports` lists every sport the site declares, in the site's order, INCLUDING sports with nothing: a sport with nothing carries null holdings, never zero-with-a-plan, and `stores` is what makes that null a measured absence rather than an unsearched one.

stores.description: Every store that was read. A null holding is a claim about exactly these stores and no others.

SportCoverage.description: One sport. Three holdings, each null when the stores hold nothing of that class for this sport. `stats` is facts about play (box scores, usage, schedules, rosters); `odds` is prices (book lines, exchange quotes, closes); `context` is everything else held as a fact about a game or player (injury reports, venues, weather, headlines). null is the ONLY way to say 'none' - a holding cannot be present and empty.

CoverageHolding.description: A class of data held for one sport. `seasons` is the union of its sources' seasons, listed rather than given as a range, because a gap is part of the claim: a range 2003-2026 would silently cover a season nobody holds.

CoverageCount.description: One table's contribution, read at `counted_at`. `units` is DISTINCT things at `grain` - games, player-games, quotes - and is the number to quote; `rows` is physical rows and exceeds it where a table keeps several versions of one fact (an upstream feed's data_version, or a superseded versioned row), so quoting rows would overstate coverage. Both are at least 1: a table that holds nothing for this sport is omitted, not published as 0.

source.description: Where the data came from, as the producer labels it: the upstream feed, or the venue and capture path.

grain.description: What one unit IS - the depth of this holding.

providers.description: Distinct books or venues inside this source, where the table records one per row; null where it does not.

season_basis.description: `column`: the table's own season field. `event_time`: derived from the event timestamp by the producer's season rule, for tables that carry no season. Stated because the second is an inference and a reader should know which they are looking at.

span.description: First and last EVENT time the table covers (a quote's capture time, a game's kickoff), where it has one.

event_dates.description: First and last EVENT DATE the table covers, for a table that records a calendar date and no instant (Retrosheet: the game's local date, no time of day). The cutoff a page states - 'box scores through 1 November 2025' - is `last`, read from the store at `counted_at`. A calendar date, not a timestamp: converting it to an instant would invent a time of day, and rendered in a US time zone a midnight-UTC instant falls on the previous day. null where the table records an instant (see `span`) or neither; `span` and `event_dates` are never both non-null.

ingested_through.description: The latest INGESTION time in the table, where it records one - as of when this holding was last written, which is not when its events happened.

retention.description: `kept`: nothing deletes these rows by age. `rolling`: a retention policy deletes them by age, so `units` is a window, not a history. Read from the producer's configured prune sources.

CoverageStore.description: A store that was read, with every sport value found in it. `tables` counts the store's tables and `classified` those the producer knows how to read or has excluded with a reason; the producer refuses unless they are equal, so a table added later cannot sit outside the count unnoticed.

PredictorFile.description: A predictor published WITH ITS SCORING RECORD, in the same file and keyed to the same slice as the values it scores. Every slice the predictor defines appears in `slices` whether or not it is published - a withheld slice is present with null figures and a reason, never absent, so a page can say why a number is missing rather than failing to notice it is. Per-subject figures are in `values` (the contract's AnalyticValue, so interval and n are mandatory); everything about a slice as a whole - its null, its separation test, its chance baseline, its scoring record, its bands - lives ONCE on the envelope under `slices[slice]` and is never repeated per row.

block.description: What every interval in this file resamples - the unit of independence. For drafting it is the draft class: a class shares a front office, a board and a year.

null_definition.description: What the null IS, in words. For a share-shaped question the null is a typical subject, not zero; the per-slice numeric value is `slices[s].null_value`.

alpha.description: The level every verdict in this file was computed at.

sources.description: Each dataset read, as `dataset@pull-date`. The pull date is the data version.

values.description: Per-subject figures, PUBLISHED SLICES ONLY. `n` is draft classes (the blocks), `rows` is picks. Order carries no claim.

attribution.description: ADDED f-07. The credit a source's terms make a condition of republishing. Sports-Reference's Terms of Use section 5 welcomes publishing its data 'but ... should explicitly credit SRL as the source of the data to the maximum extent possible'; every drafting slice rests on PFR's draft table, so the file carries it and a page must render `statement` wherever any slice in `applies_to` is shown. Null only for a predictor with no source that asks for credit.

values_policy.description: ADDED f-07. Whether per-subject values are published for a slice that does not separate on what it names. An EDITORIAL choice, recorded so a page can say which one it is reading: `show` publishes every published slice's values; `hide` publishes values only where `reading` is `separates`, and every other published slice keeps its slice-level figures with `values_reason` set.

PredictorSlice.description: One slice of a predictor. Definitional fields (label, unit, direction, null_value, window) are always present. Every MEASURED field is null when `status` is `withheld`, and `withheld_reasons` then says why; when `published`, `withheld_reasons` is empty and the measured fields are present (though `record.score` and `bands` may still be null, each with its own reason).

withheld_reasons.description: `licence_unresolved`: a source's redistribution terms have not been read (none today: f-07 read Sports-Reference's). `confounded`: the slice separates subjects on something other than what the predictor names. Empty when published.

unit.description: What one value IS, in words.

cannot_see.description: What this measure is blind to, in words.

null_value.description: The numeric null a value is read against. A typical subject, not zero, unless the two coincide by construction (they do for drafting: residuals are centred within each class).

chance.description: How many subjects' intervals exclude the null, against how many do so under shuffled labels - MEASURED, because a percentile block bootstrap over 10-21 blocks runs narrow and the nominal alpha x subjects understates chance.

confound.description: Correlation of the subject's value with an outcome it must NOT be measuring (for drafting: team regular-season win share). A large one means the slice cannot separate the predictor from the confound.

bands.description: Bands against each band's LEADER, never against the row above: the best remaining subject leads, every subject whose contrast with it (bootstrapped as one quantity over shared blocks) covers zero joins it, repeat. Array order runs best band first and is the only order; there is NO band number and NO rank within a band. `members` is alphabetical and includes the leader. NULL whenever the separation test does not reject - the leader is a selected maximum and its contrasts are unadjusted, so bands can split a population that cannot be told from shuffled labels. When null, a page lists the values as one unordered, alphabetical set.

bands_reason.description: Why `bands` is null; null when bands are present.

reading.description: ADDED f-07. The slice's one-word verdict, computed from `separation`, `record` and `confound`, and what a page leads with. `separates`: subjects separate and no named confound explains it. `separates_confounded`: they separate, but the measure is confounded BY CONSTRUCTION (named in the producer) and the measured confound excludes zero - it is NOT a finding about the predictor's subject. `does_not_separate`: they do not, and the record says nothing more. `forecasts` / `forecasts_inversely` / `not_readable`: they do not separate and the record's verdict is this. Null only when withheld.

statement.description: ADDED f-07. One sentence GENERATED from this slice's figures at export time, naming its separation, its confound and its forecast together, so none of the three can be quoted without the others. Render verbatim or not at all. Null only when withheld.

values_reason.description: ADDED f-07. Why this slice has no rows in `values`; null when it has them. `separation_not_rejected` / `confounded`: published slice, values held back under `values_policy` = `hide`. `withheld`: the slice itself is withheld.

allOf.description: A PUBLISHED slice carries its scoring record - never null, never absent - and its measurement, its `reading` and its `statement`, and names no withheld reason; its `values_reason` is never `withheld`. This is what makes 'every predictor ships with its record visible' a property of the file rather than a promise: a published slice with `record: null` does not validate. The record may still say it was never scored (`score` null), but then it must say why.

A WITHHELD slice names at least one reason and carries no measured field - no `reading` or `statement` either, since both are computed from the measurement - and its `values_reason` is `withheld`, so a withheld number cannot leak through a slice marked withheld.
`bands_reason` is present exactly when `bands` is null.

rows.description: Picks. Not the sample; published beside it.

unresolved_rows.description: Rows that could not be joined to an outcome and are scored as zero rather than dropped.

PredictorSeparation.description: Do subjects differ by more than shuffled labels would? Between-subject SD of values against a permutation null that shuffles subject labels within each block. `verdict` is computed from `p` against the file's `alpha` and can take either value.

PredictorRecord.description: THE SCORING RECORD. `score` is how the predictor did when it was used to forecast outcomes it could not see; it is NULL when the slice has never been scored, and `reason` says why - it is never simply absent. For drafting the score is a walk-forward Pearson r: a subject's record over blocks whose horizon had closed predicts its next block, averaged over targets, interval by bootstrapping targets.

lag_blocks.description: How many blocks back the forecast had to stop to see no open horizon.

verdict.description: Computed from the interval against 0 and `n` against `min_readable_n`. `forecasts`: excludes 0 above. `forecasts_inversely`: excludes 0 below. `no_better_than_chance`: covers 0. `not_readable`: too few targets for the interval to be read at all, whatever it excludes.

reason.description: Why `score` is null. `not_as_of`: the outcome is a snapshot total with no version knowable at forecast time, so no forecast can be scored against it. Null when a score is present.

allOf.description: A null `score` must carry a `reason`; a present `score` must not. Unscored is allowed and must be stated, never implied by absence.

SourcesFile.description: Every upstream source a sport's files read, GENERATED from jobs/source_registry.py rather than written (a-22, audit S-04). `sources` is the union of what the kinds declare; `kinds` maps every contract kind to the source_ids it reads for this sport, so a page can refuse a kind whose sources are not listed; `not_connected` is what the producer does not export, with the state it is in.

last_read.description: When the pipeline last read this source successfully. Null when this export does not measure it, and `last_read_basis` then says why.

BoardIndexFile.description: One week's Board: every read taken, which is latest, the lean threshold in force and the week's ledger counts. Written by the Board read job at every read, beside the read file it names. `leans` counts the ledger's four-way partition for this week - every published lean is in exactly one of graded, upcoming, live, void - so a lean that has left the board (its main line moved, its market was pulled) is still counted here.

reads.description: Every read of this week, ascending. Each names a board_read file.

lean_threshold_pp.description: T in force at the latest read, probability points.

lean_threshold_log.description: Every threshold ever in force: [effective from, T, why]. A change is appended, never edited, so a lean is always graded against the T it was published under.

BoardVerdict.description: The walk-forward record the verdict strip quotes: Brier(model) - Brier(close) with its interval and the games it was bootstrapped over. The interval and `games` are REQUIRED AND NOT NULLABLE, for the reason AnalyticValue gives: the consumer words the verdict from the interval and must refuse a bare number rather than trust the producer.

games.description: Independent units the interval was built on: games, not predictions.

BoardReadFile.description: One Board read: every row as the books and the model stood at `read_at`. A read is never rewritten; the next read is a new file. Rows are keyed across reads by `claim_id` (one player, one market, one game); `row_id` names the main line at THIS read and changes when the line moves.

rows.description: Never empty: a read that found nothing is refused by the producer and never written, because an empty read is indistinguishable from a broken one.

is_main.description: True when `line` is the main line at this read - a property of the read, not of the market. False only on a row kept because it carries a published lean whose line the main line has since moved off (line_moved_after_publication).

ladder.description: Every threshold the benchmark books listed at this read.

mkt_p_over.description: Median across the benchmark books of each book's multiplicatively de-vigged P(over) at `line`. A price, not an estimate from a sample: `mkt_books` says how many books it is the median of.

kalshi_mid.description: The exchange's mid on the same claim, as-is and never de-vigged. Null when no mapped exchange market was quoted.

model_p_over.description: The model's P(over) at this read. Null for a market the model does not price, or a fit that failed.

gap_pp.description: Model minus market, probability points, signed. Null when either side is null.

lean_price.description: Median American price on the lean side across the benchmark books at this read.

band.description: The walk-forward base rate for leans this size in this market. Null when the row carries no lean, or when the walk-forward has no record for the band - never an object with no sample.

news.description: Empty until a news source is ingested. Not faked.

void_reason.description: Present exactly when status is void, so a voided row can never be mistaken for a quietly dropped one.

pulled_at.description: The read at which the books stopped listing the claim; null unless void_reason is market_pulled.

priced_at.description: The read whose books this row's market fields (ladder, books, mkt_p_over, kalshi_mid, model_p_over, gap_pp, lean_price, band, line_path) describe. Equal to the file's read_at on a row priced at this read; earlier on a row frozen at kickoff, or kept because it carries a published lean the current read no longer reproduces.

line_moved_after_publication.description: This row carries a published lean and the main line has since moved off its line, so the row is kept as priced at `priced_at` and graded on its own line. The market moving away from a lean is shown, never hidden: the lean stays on the board (a-34).

lean_changed_after_publication.description: This row carries a published lean, the main line is still its line, and the current read no longer leans that way at it. Kept as priced at `priced_at` and graded on its own line (a-34).

BoardBook.description: One benchmark book's two-way quote at `line`, as that book last showed it. Prices are American odds.

BoardBand.description: The walk-forward record of leans this size: how often they cleared and what they returned at the price that stood. EVERY ESTIMATE CARRIES A NON-NULLABLE INTERVAL AND AN INTEGER SAMPLE - the AnalyticValue rule. `n` is LEANS and `ci` is a Wilson interval on leans; `games` is the independent unit, and `roi_ci` is a game-block bootstrap over it. The two sample sizes are published together because only one of them is the sample the Wilson interval assumes.

cleared.description: Against TODAY's line. Null when the value is null or exactly on the line.

BoardRates.description: The player's record against today's line (last10, season, career) and against each game's own posted line (career_posted). Each is null when there is no graded game in it - never a record with n = 0.

BoardRate.description: k of n games cleared, with a Wilson interval. `n` is games - one graded game per row - and never zero.

basis.description: How many of the n games took their market at the close from the benchmark-book median, and how many from every book.

BoardStreak.description: A streak rule that fired against today's line, and the measured rate at which the NEXT game cleared after the same rule fired. `display_rate` is the streak as a reader sees it; `next_rate` is the estimate, with its interval and sample, and they differ by design.

next_n.description: Streak instances the next-game rate was measured on.

LabRate.description: k of n graded bets cleared, with a Wilson interval. `n` counts BETS, and the Wilson interval treats them as independent, which they are not quite (bets in one week share game-level shocks); the ROI and units intervals beside it are week-block bootstrapped for that reason. Null in place of this object when nothing was graded - never an object with n = 0.

LabBootstrap.description: An ROI (profit over staked) or a units total (profit over the unit stake) with a percentile interval from resampling whole WEEKS (`blocks` of them) `draws` times. `n` is the staked bets: cleared, missed and pushed; voids stake nothing. Null in place of this object when it is withheld or nothing was staked.

LabWithheld.description: Why ROI and units are absent, or null when they are published. They are withheld wherever they would average fewer than `min_cleared` cleared bets' prices: an ROI over one cleared bet, published beside its counts, IS that bet's book price, and book prices do not leave the server.

LabCell.description: One row of a by-season or segment breakdown. `thin` marks fewer than 100 bets, where the interval is wide enough that the row should not be read on its own.

LabVerdict.description: The verdict chip, by fixed rule in lab.engine.verdict - never judgement. LOSES: the ROI interval is below zero. WORTH A FORWARD TEST: above zero with the holdout unrevealed. SURVIVED / FAILED HOLDOUT: above zero, holdout revealed, holdout ROI above / at or below zero. NO EVIDENCE OF EDGE: the interval spans zero and the luck check sits inside 5-95. UNCLEAR: spans zero, luck outside 5-95 or not computable. NO BETS: nothing graded.

LabLuck.description: The luck check: the same number of bets drawn at random from the same universe and side, `draws` times, flat stakes. `percentile` is where the rule's flat ROI falls among them; `band` reads it against 5 and 95. Null percentile, with `note` saying why, when the rule takes every bet the universe offers (a random draw of the same size IS the rule). `paths` is the 5th-95th percentile band of the random draws' cumulative units at `index` bets - the draws', never the rule's own curve.

LabPresetFile.description: One Lab library preset, run by lab.run over the universe table (the same code a user's rule runs) and published as AGGREGATES ONLY - no service. The holdout is the Lab's default: the latest complete season held out and NOT revealed, so no figure here includes it. `bet_list` deliberately carries no book price, book, stake or profit, and there is no equity curve: see `bet_list.restriction`, which is the reason in the file itself.

strategy.description: lab.strategy/1 exactly as the engine approved it, defaults filled. The shape is DERIVED from lab/strategy.schema.json by jobs.lab_publish.contract_strategy (sport as a plain string, maxLength dropped, a condition value typed as a scalar or a list of scalars) and tests/test_lab_publish.py asserts the derivation, so it is never edited by hand.

statement.description: One line, generated by lab.strategy.check from the strategy it approved.

break_even.description: 1 / the mean decimal price paid over staked bets: the hit rate at which this rule's ROI is zero. Withheld with ROI.

mean_devig_prob.description: Mean de-vigged probability of the side bet, over graded bets.

provenance.description: Where each season's prices came from, one entry per season, ascending. `is_close` is false for the free games-schedule line, which is one line per game from a provider not verified per season, never labelled a close.

restriction.description: Why this list carries no book price, book, stake or profit. Deliberate; do not add them back without a decision that The Odds API's terms allow it.

columns.description: The name of each position in a row, in order.

LabIndexEntry.description: One launch preset. `published` names its lab_preset file. `unsupported` means the engine cannot run it and says why in `reasons` - the engine's own refusal where it refused, or the language's limit where a rule has two legs - so the Library shows it as known-and-excluded rather than silently missing. `register` cites the register row that measures it elsewhere, when one does.

LabIndexFile.description: The Lab library: every preset in the audit's launch set, in its order, published or not. Written on every run of jobs/lab_publish.py, and names every lab_preset file it wrote.

min_cleared.description: The fewest cleared bets an ROI may average over before it is published.
